- **Status:** Landed; default bt2100; playback test open.
- `--hlg-composer bt2100` (2026-10-03) is fitted to the BT.2100 / BT.2408 1000-nit HLG-to-PQ
  conversion and keeps neutrals neutral; the HLG colour input contract is enforced. Design and
  measurements: [`docs/HLG_COMPOSER.md`](docs/HLG_COMPOSER.md). The preset it replaces tints
  neutrals (75% grey ΔE_ITP 6.8, up to 10.3 near black) and decodes nominal white to about
  1150 nits.
- **Open:** the WS6 playback test must show that devices apply a composer that is not the preset,
  and how visible the tint is on a TV. 4:2:0 chroma siting of the analyzer's decode (both

  since 2026-10-05 (live sport at 50p, a concert, a nature series, a broadcast capture, a drama;
  WS8 item 5).

expect.description: `chroma-siting` argument parsing accepts a width or height of 0 (it only checks that both are even), so with a zero dimension the frame buffer is empty and the frame-read loop never advances: the tool loops forever instead of refusing the input.
The real-cut summary globs every `cut-*` directory in the work dir, so with a reused `--keep` directory it also reports (and judges) cuts measured by an earlier run that this run did not measure.

The script hard-codes the local development-corpus directory names (`HLG_CUTS=(g1-wimbledon-2024-final-rally ... d11-bluelights-s01e02-hlg)`) in a committed file, against the repo rule that corpus media and their file names stay local; it should discover HLG cuts from each cut's manifest.json.

The /roadmap-next confirm mode reuses the stored (unscoped) Next up ranking whenever nothing relevant changed, even when the run was given a scope argument, so a scoped run returns the unscoped ranking instead of ranking afresh.

- **Status:** Landed; default bt2100; playback test open.
- `--hlg-composer bt2100` (2026-10-03) is fitted to the BT.2100 / BT.2408 1000-nit HLG-to-PQ
  conversion and keeps neutrals neutral; the HLG colour input contract is enforced. Design and
  measurements: [`docs/HLG_COMPOSER.md`](docs/HLG_COMPOSER.md). The preset it replaces tints
  neutrals (75% grey ΔE_ITP 6.8, up to 10.3 near black) and decodes nominal white to about
  1150 nits.
- **Open:** the WS6 playback test must show that devices apply a composer that is not the preset,
  and how visible the tint is on a TV. Real HLG material for both: five cuts since 2026-10-05
  (live sport at 50p, a concert, a nature series, a broadcast capture, a drama; WS8 item 5).
- **Open: spec 4:2:0 decode in the analyzer** (both composers). Measured 2026-10-05
  ([`docs/HLG_COMPOSER.md`](docs/HLG_COMPOSER.md) §9): the analyzer replicates chroma over the
  quad and reshapes it with each pixel's own luma in `code / 1023` float; the spec composer runs
  the MMR at chroma resolution on down-sampled luma in `code / 1024` fixed point. Per scene on the
  HLG cuts that moves L1 max by up to 18 codes and the average by up to 5, above the 4-code limit.
  The change must: take the spec's structure and arithmetic (the tool's `spec-fixed` variant);
  choose and justify an upsampler for the composed chroma, which the spec leaves to the display
  (replicated against bilinear: 6.5 against 18.3 codes of L1 max on one cut); re-check the
  `bt2100` neutral criteria under the spec's arithmetic; keep CPU and CUDA identical. It moves HLG
  L1 for every file, so it needs a new `luminance_mapping` name, re-analysis of older sidecars and
  its own branch. Gate: the analyzer reproduces the tool's `spec-fixed` variant within 0.5 code per
  frame on the synthetic patterns and the five cuts (`scripts/validate_hlg_chroma_siting.sh`).
  The script does not enforce that gate yet: it fails only on its anchors, which compare the
  analyzer with the tool's `analyzer` variant, so the fix must first make `spec-fixed` decide.
- **Checked 2026-10-06 @ab13527:** the script's failures are anchor 1 (tool `analyzer` variant,
  `validate_hlg_chroma_siting.sh:313`), anchor 2 and unmodelled locations; `spec-fixed` is only
  printed (`:339`, `:367`), a missing cut is skipped (`:263`) and `--every` thins frames. Nothing
  carries the chroma location to the analysis (`ffmpeg_io.rs` `VideoInfo`, `frame.rs`
  `FrameAnalysisOptions`). The tool's fixed point uses i128 (`siting.rs:238`), the kernel f32.

expect.description: The gate's Python reads each `runs` record with `line.split()` into four fields; a `--keep` work directory whose path contains spaces makes the stem split into extra fields, so the gate crashes with a ValueError after the whole (hours-long) analysis has run.

The letterbox-clip runs in the P8 gate only get the per-pixel comparison; the sidecar checks (luminance_mapping is the composer's current name, and `analysis.gpu` matches the requested backend) run only inside `check_run`, which the letterbox runs skip. A `--hwaccel cuda` letterbox run that silently fell back to the CPU, or carries the wrong mapping, would still pass the gate.

## What and why

PR #34 deferred this hardening. On 2026-10-07 the Gemini pre-PR pass failed after 41 s. Gemini tried to read a file under `~/.claude/` that the diff names, print mode denied the read, and the denial ended the run. The pass also had no retry, no idle watchdog (only `timeout 900`), and recorded no cost data for the reviewer-yield tally.

`.claude/workflows/pre-pr-gemini.sh` now has:
- **Tool-limited agent.** The repo agent `.agents/agents/pre-pr-reviewer.md` (`--agent`) allows only `view_file`, `grep_search` and `finish`. Terminal commands, writes and web access are gone from the tool set. `finish` is required, or `--json-schema` returns no `structured_output`.
- **One retry, with a new nonce.** It covers:
  - a denial; the new prompt names the denied path or tool and never contains a nonce;
  - a stall;
  - a missing or malformed result;
  - a nonce mismatch;
  - a status other than SUCCESS;
  - a retryable `AGY_ERROR`.

  The retry runs only when at least 300 s remain. Startup, quota and auth errors are not retried.
- **Idle watchdog.** An attempt stops after 480 s without a write to its stream, its stderr or agy's conversation store (`conversations/<id>.db-wal`). A probe showed a thinking step that kept the stream silent for 341 s while the WAL was written at least every 19 s. `PRE_PR_GEMINI_TIMEOUT` goes from 900 to 1200 s and now covers all attempts.
- **Cleanup.** It kills the process group and every process that carries the attempt's environment marker, including children that start their own session. A `timeout` backstop inside the session ends agy 60 s after the deadline even if the wrapper is SIGKILLed. INT, TERM and HUP end the pass with an `interrupted` result, and a second signal during cleanup is ignored.
- **Telemetry.** The result keeps its old keys and adds `attempts[]` (outcome, seconds, steps, tokens, `denied_path`/`denied_tool`) and `usage` totals. Usage is marked `partial` when agy's own report is missing.

Related changes:
- `pre-pr-panel.js` computes a `gemini-harness` gate for the Gemini-pass paths.
- The pre-PR record gets `geminiCost` for the yield tally.
- CLAUDE.md and the `pre-pr-review` skill are updated.

These contracts do not change: the script always exits 0, the nonce check stays, print mode stays `--mode plan --sandbox`, the diff stays inline on stdin, and the model stays `gemini-3.8-flash-medium`.

I did not adopt `yuting0624/antigravity-for-claude-code`. It is a general delegation wrapper with a wall-clock timeout and no watchdog, nonce or schema check.

expect.description: Race in the watchdog poll loop: after each `sleep $poll; wait $!` the loop goes straight to the idle and deadline checks without rechecking that agy is still running, so an agy run that completed during the last poll interval (e.g. one that crosses the deadline while sleeping) is killed/classified as a timeout or stall and its valid result is discarded.

spec:
## Problem

When MediaInfo is missing or names no HDR format, `check_hdr_format` and `has_hlg_transfer` fall back to ffprobe. That fallback read only the stream-level `color_transfer`, which usually carries the HEVC VUI value. HLG signalled only through the alternative transfer characteristics SEI (broadcast HLG) was therefore missed:

- conversion: `Detected: Unsupported`, input refused;
- `--mdfix` on such a Profile 8.4 file: not refused upfront; it re-analyzed and then failed at the L1 sidecar check with a misleading "input is not HLG" error.

Stream level vs first decoded frame, ffprobe 6.1 (apt) and 9.0.2:

| Input | Stream 6.1 | Stream 9.0.2 | Frame (both) |
|---|---|---|---|
| d11 BBC Blue Lights | `arib-std-b67` | `bt2020-10` | `arib-std-b67` |
| g1 Wimbledon | `bt2020-10` | `bt2020-10` | `arib-std-b67` |
| g4 UCL Bayern–PSG | `bt709` | `bt709` | `arib-std-b67` |
| x265 `atc-sei=18` clip, MKV | `bt2020-10` | `bt2020-10` | `arib-std-b67` |

So this is not an FFmpeg 9 regression. The stream-level value depends on the file and container.

## Fix

`ffprobe_indicates_hlg` checks the stream-level tags, then reads the first decoded frame's transfer (`first_frame_color_transfer`, which already exists for the VUI-rewrite check) when no stream tag names HLG. `has_hlg_transfer` and the `check_hdr_format` fallback (`ffprobe_hdr_format`) both use it. The extra ffprobe call only runs on the fallback path.

expect.description: The ffprobe fallback looks at every stream instead of only the first video stream: `ffprobe_indicates_hlg` (line 94) returns HLG if ANY stream's color_transfer is HLG, and `ffprobe_hdr_format` checks that before classifying (line 80) and then classifies the first recognized transfer of any stream (lines 83-84). A file whose first video track (0:v:0, the one the conversion extracts and the frame probe reads) is PQ but has a second HLG video track is detected as HLG and converted as Profile 8.4.

specSource: Fix without a roadmap step: the '## Problem' and '## Fix' sections of the PR body (before '## Verification'), `gh pr view 43 -R tinof/hdr-analyze --json body -q .body | sed -n 1,22p`.

The contract: detection must look at the same stream the conversion extracts (0:v:0) and the first-frame probe reads. At preFixHead the unit test `stream_transfers_lists_tagged_streams_only` in mkvdovi/src/metadata/tests.rs pins the multi-stream behaviour. The plan note's second location (format.rs:95, codex-steered: first packet not a random-access picture gives no first frame) was REJECTED in the review record and never fixed, so it is not an expect entry; a reviewer reporting it should not be credited for this defect. ### E16: in-process RPU builders

- **Status:** Open. E16.1 shipped `dovi_rpu_builder` (#67). A review from the NuvioTV fork (its
  `ROADMAP_LOG.md`, 2026-10-23) found that `RpuBuilder::new`
  (`dovi_rpu_builder/src/builder.rs:93`) accepts parameters that every later `ShotRpu::write`
  refuses as the generic `Error::Rpu`: L6 above 10 000, L5 offsets above 8191, L9
  `source_primary_index` 255, L11 `content_type` above 15, more than 8 trim targets, an 8.1 source
  range above 4095. An empty or inverted 8.1 source range is written without complaint. The docs
  overstate `panic = "abort"` (it covers this workspace only), omit the L3 and L254 that every CM
  v4.0 RPU carries, and tell callers to reset the HDR10+ scene hold after a seek, which is the
  caller's policy.
- [E16.2][desk] Validate in `RpuBuilder::new`: refuse those values (and an empty or inverted 8.1
  source range) as `Error::OutOfRange`, with a backstop write of the base so a builder that exists
  writes every shot; add `Level6::clamped` for SEI values and `Error::code` for JNI; correct the
  three doc points. No delivered RPU, `extra.json` or mkvdovi output changes. Gate: unit tests at
  10001, 8192, 9 targets, L9 255, L11 16 and a 4096, empty and inverted source range fail on the
  parent and get `Error::OutOfRange` from `new`; values at the limits write; the fixture tests and
  the live `dovi_tool` test stay byte-identical; the repo gate and `tool:rpu_builder_check` pass.

expect.description: The new trim-target limit in RpuBuilder::new / the V40 block builder counts raw trim_targets_nits entries (len() > MAX_TRIM_TARGETS = 8). The dolby_vision crate merges L2 blocks that share a target_max_pq (CmV29DmData::replace_level2_block), so e.g. nine targets that map to eight distinct PQ codes (a duplicate nits value) write fine, but new() now refuses them with Error::OutOfRange: a regression that refuses valid input and breaks the 'new refuses exactly what write would refuse' invariant.

chore(release): draft-first release workflow, release rules and pre-flight

- release.yml: check (tag = manifests = Cargo.lock, dated CHANGELOG section) -> test (CI's
  fmt/clippy incl. cuda, full suite with ffmpeg/mkvtoolnix/mediainfo/pinned dovi_tool, fails on
  unexpected skips) -> build (adds Linux ARM64; binaries must report the tag) -> publish
  (SHA256SUMS, actions/attest, draft with all assets, then publish; -rc.N = pre-release).
  Notes come from the CHANGELOG section instead of the stale v0.3.0 text. PRs touching the
  release machinery dry-run everything except publish.
- scripts/ci/release-version-check.sh, release-notes.sh, check-test-skips.sh;
  scripts/release-check.sh (local read-only pre-flight).
- docs/RELEASING.md (terms, version rules, when to release, checklist, runbook, repo settings),
  ROADMAP.md Release plan, roadmap-next keeps Release tags and the plan current.
- install.sh installs the Linux ARM64 archive.

expect.description: The generated release notes' upgrade section says a mkvdovi_temp_* directory left by another version is not resumed and the conversion starts again. That is wrong for temp dirs without a resume.json fingerprint (made before 0.4.0, or legacy mkvdolby_temp_*): resume.rs resumes those with a warning, so the note contradicts mkvdovi's resume contract.

The release workflow's cargo calls run without --locked (the release build at line 173, and also the clippy calls at 97/99 and the test-job build/test at 117/118), so a Cargo.lock that does not match the manifests is silently re-resolved per runner and release binaries can be built from dependency versions other than the committed lock file.

The version check only requires a dated '## [X.Y.Z] - date' heading in CHANGELOG.md; an empty section (heading with no entries, e.g. entries left under [Unreleased]) passes, so the release (and the pre-flight scripts/release-check.sh:41 that calls this script) can publish a release with empty notes.

The pull_request paths filter that triggers the release dry run omits .cargo/config.toml (the aarch64 Linux linker setting) and rust-toolchain.toml, which affect release builds that ci.yml never builds (ARM64 Linux, macOS Intel); a PR changing them merges without any release dry run.

The local pre-flight checks only that ci.yml passed on HEAD. The release gate (integration tests with their tools, all five builds) runs only in release.yml, whose PR trigger skips Cargo.lock/manifest changes, so a tag can be pushed for a commit on which release.yml never ran; the pre-flight does not require a release.yml dry run (workflow_dispatch) on HEAD.

spec:
### P9: HDR10+ → Profile 8.1 L1

- **Status:** Open; step 0 (frame alignment) done 2026-10-08; scene list chosen 2026-10-13.
- `dovi_tool generate --hdr10plus-json` takes L1 from the first frame of each HDR10+ scene
  (minimum 0, average rounded to whole nits, no measured crop). On the HDR10+ test cut the average
  reads 156 to 505 codes above the analyzer's mean; the cause is not separated.
- **Prerequisite met (2026-10-05):** four HDR10+ titles from two studios and one streamer
  (WS8 item 5). Alita: Battle Angel carries Dolby Vision MEL and HDR10+ on the same disc, so its
  retail L1 can score an HDR10+-derived L1 frame by frame.
- **Finding for the fallback:** both HDR10+ Profile A discs (Alien, Alita) carry MaxSCL 0 on every
  frame, but the percentile distribution (99th percentile 90 to 129 nits per scene on Alita) and
  the average are present. A peak taken from MaxSCL is unusable on such sources, so the pixel
  fallback is required, not optional; whether the percentiles can stand in is open.
- **Plan:** opt-in hybrid mode (scene list = union of HDR10+ starts and the analyzer's cuts, peak
  per piece from HDR10+; average, minimum and L5 from pixels),
  scored on the development tier before any default change, with a pixel fallback for missing or
  implausible HDR10+ statistics. The panel peak is still not passed as a trim target, and
  suspicious scene peaks still only warn.
- **Done 2026-10-08: step 0, HDR10+ scene boundaries against the picture.** HDR10+ frame n is
  picture frame n: offset 0 on all six multi-scene HDR10+ cuts (five by the scan, one by
  corroboration), no confirmed off-by-one (Alien 298 ambiguous), v5 runs and mkvdovi's extraction path
  ([log](docs/ROADMAP_LOG.md) 2026-10-08). The scene list is not a shot
  list: 24% of the frames sit in HDR10+ scenes holding more than one shot (Alita, The Shining), and
  some HDR10+ starts split a shot (Alien).
- **Done 2026-10-13: which scene list carries the pixel average.** The union of HDR10+ starts and
  the analyzer's cuts, by the pre-registered rule; the HDR10+ scenes, the analyzer's cuts and the
  union score within about 1.5 codes of each other (pooled clamped MAE above the floor 38.3 / 36.8 /
  37.6), and the analyzer's cuts are the numerical best. The gain is the measured average itself:
  pooled clamped MAE over all frames 18.9 codes against 338.4 for today's HDR10+ path, which writes
  1229 where retail sits at the 819 floor. The 18.9 holds after the generator's 819 floor; raw, the
  measured average is 147.6 codes off over all frames (about 259 below on floor frames). Two cuts from one title; peak and minimum not
  evaluated ([log](docs/ROADMAP_LOG.md) 2026-10-13).
- **Open:** the hybrid flag (E13 step 4 done 2026-10-13; the analyzer seam is `pipeline/measure.rs`): the union carries average and minimum; peak per piece
  from HDR10+ with the pixel fallback; its integration gate needs an HDR10+-only cut (Alita takes the
  MEL path). Before a default change (owner list): score holdout HDR10+ cuts, where the union could
  show whether HDR10+ starts rescue cuts the analyzer misses; none did on the development cuts.
- **Checked 2026-10-14 @ae211e6:** seam `pipeline/measure.rs:140` (HDR10+ runs no analyzer),
  `dovi_steps.rs:322` passes `--hdr10plus-json`, `pipeline/mod.rs:275` drops the sidecar from
  verify. mkvdovi's `L1SidecarFrames` reads only `min_pq_12bit` (`metadata/sidecar.rs:179`), and the
  sidecar has no per-frame max (`l1_sidecar.rs:146`), so the flag extends the reader and takes the
  fallback peak from the `.bin` or a sidecar v6. `rpu_config.rs:200` already shifts by leading
  pictures: shift the union once. v5 runs: `~/mkvdovi-work/p9-step0-2026-10-08`.

expect.description: check_measurements (and its doc) treats the L1 sidecar as proof that max-RGB scene peaks are the plain maximum (the hybrid's fallback peak), but the sidecar does not record the analyzer's own --peak-source: measurements made with e.g. --peak-source histogram99 pass the peak_domain/peak_estimator checks and their scene peak is a luma percentile. Either 'the check cannot verify the peak source' or 'the doc overclaims what the sidecar proves' is this defect; the fix only corrected the doc and deferred a real check to a sidecar v6.

The HDR10+ SceneFrameNumbers consistency check computes start + length == end on u64 values from the HDR10+ JSON; a malformed length near u64::MAX overflows (panic in debug builds, wrap in release) instead of being refused as inconsistent.

clap's conflicts_with = "legacy_madvr_l1" on --hdr10plus-l1 also fires when the default value is given explicitly, so '--hdr10plus-l1 hdr10plus --legacy-madvr-l1' is rejected although only 'hybrid' conflicts with --legacy-madvr-l1.

### P11: `--mdfix` and authored metadata

- **Status:** Open; decided 2026-10-13 (owner): full regeneration stays, with a notice.
- `--mdfix` regenerates the whole RPU: authored L2 and L4 become neutral L2 and no L4, authored L5
  is reduced to one sampled value, L6 comes from the container. Retail trims are far from neutral.
- **Decision (owner, 2026-10-13):** keep full regeneration, since trims were authored for the
  authored L1 and shot list; no targeted repair. **Open:** `--mdfix` states in its output which
  authored levels it drops.
- **Checked 2026-10-14 @f5d4ccc:** samplers `rpu_check::extract_rpu_sample` (`rpu_check.rs:132`,
  from `metadata/format.rs:468`) and `sample_rpu_windows` (`rpu_check.rs:182`, from
  `pipeline/measure.rs:50`); `SampledRpu` (`rpu_check.rs:173`) has no L2/L4. Name each level by what
  happens: L1, L2, L6, L9, L11 regenerated (`generate_extra_json`, `metadata/rpu_config.rs:103`);
  L3 replaced by neutral offsets (2048) and L254 added (`dovi_tool` CM v4.0 defaults, seen in the
  0.6.0 `--mdfix` baselines); L4, L8, L10 removed; L5 reduced to one sampled value. To name them,
  the sampler must also detect L2/L3/L4/L8. A sampled absence means "not seen"; a failed read
  still gives a general notice.

expect.description: l8_target_label asks the crate's preset lookup (ExtMetadataBlockLevel8::trim_target_nits) first and returns its nits whenever it is not 100, and only then consults the sampled L10 that defines a custom target display. An L10 may define a custom display at any non-preset index, including 24 and 25, which the crate reads as 300 nits, so the --mdfix notice mislabels such a custom L8 trim target as '300 nits' instead of its L10 peak.

### E14: test-suite audit

- **Status:** Open; step 1 (PR CI runs the tool-dependent tests) in review 2026-10-15. Rules:
  [`docs/TESTING.md`](docs/TESTING.md).
- **Why:** a test that has never been red has not been shown to test anything. Until 2026-10-15
  the PR CI test job installed none of the integration-test tools, so the HLG 8.4, open-GOP, P7
  full-range refusal (`pq_input_contract`), HDR10+ hybrid, synthetic-accuracy and clip tests
  passed as skips (0.00 s on main run 38715765973); only `release.yml` ran them. Mutation testing ran once (E13 step 2: 69 of 75
  `metadata.rs` mutants caught) and was never repeated. A read-only sweep on 2026-10-15
  (`~/mkvdovi-work/test-audit-2026-10-15/smells-*.md`, unverified) lists one-sided decisions
  (`classify_rpu_format`, the `inject_rpu` length refusal, `hlg_bitstream_lacks_transfer`, the
  verifier's accept path), assertions that only check `is_ok()`, and tests that restate the
  production formula.
- **Steps:**
  1. PR CI installs the tools (`.github/actions/setup-test-tools`, shared with `release.yml`) and
     fails on unexpected skips.
  2. P13 pilot: Codex writes the P13 acceptance tests from a behaviour-only spec in a worktree
     without the diagnosis; record whether they assert something an in-session test would not,
     and the cost. The owner decides whether a separate test author becomes a roadmap step.
  3. Mutation baseline (`cargo-mutants`) on `mkvdovi/src`, `verifier/src`,
     `dovi84_composer/src` and the analyzer contract files (`l1_sidecar.rs`,
     `leading_pictures.rs`, `ffmpeg_io.rs`, `writer.rs`, `cli.rs`), after a clean
     `check-test-skips` baseline on the host. Analyzer numerics wait for E13 step 5; E8 is then the
     validation case.
  4. Triage every survivor (missing test / equivalent / actual bug / dead code /
     characterization); actual-bug survivors go to the owner before any test.
  5. Test-only PRs per crate area; each new test names the mutant it kills or the decision side it
     adds.
  6. After the pilot: a `cargo mutants --in-diff` gate in the pre-PR panel for mkvdovi, verifier
     and dovi84_composer logic (fails only on infrastructure errors; survivors listed with their
     bucket), and red-on-parent evidence for fix PRs.
- **Acceptance evidence:** a clean `check-test-skips` log on the audit host; per-module mutant
  counts (caught / missed / unviable / timeout) before and after; every survivor in a bucket.

### WS6: final-RPU corpus and playback procedure

- **Status:** Open.
- Final-RPU regression corpus covering grain, saturated highlights, raised blacks, fades, flashes,
  rapid cuts and changing aspect ratios; checks run on the RPU extracted from the muxed file.
- A Shield/TV playback procedure comparing matched material from the same master, recording player,
  firmware, TV picture mode and HDMI path. It is the gate for P8, the WS6 normalization question
  and P10's device steps.
- **Gate:** (owner, 2026-10-17) (1) `scripts/rpu-baseline.sh` holds one captured baseline per
  listed feature; (2) the procedure is written (a docs section plus a `VIEWING_GUIDE.txt`
  template recording player, firmware, picture mode and HDMI path) and used once, for (3); (3) a
  discriminating canary, a composer that is neutral under one normalization and visibly coloured
  under the other, checked in libplacebo first, viewed on the LG OLED C9, answer recorded.
- The `code / 1023` question below: the first canary gave no verdict (2026-10-17, below); next, a
  canary within the coefficient range real RPUs use, preceded by a slope ladder that shows how
  steep a chroma curve the C9 still follows. Claude builds each, checks it in libplacebo and hands
  the files to the owner (owner decision 2026-10-17); the canary is designed from what the ladder
  showed, so build and viewing alternate (WS6.3 to WS6.6).
- [WS6.3][desk] Build the slope ladder. Gate: the ladder checked in libplacebo and handed off for
  the C9 with a `VIEWING_GUIDE.txt`.
- **Done 2026-10-17: (2) the written playback procedure,** [`docs/PLAYBACK.md`](docs/PLAYBACK.md),
  used for the WS6 and P10 viewings and corrected afterwards with what they showed (owner asked
  Claude to make the corrections).
- **The `code / 1023` question (2026-10-06):** do devices evaluate the 8.4 composer at `code / 1023` (as
  libplacebo and the `bt2100` fit) or at the spec's `code / 1024`? Under the latter `bt2100` is
  5.9 codes off neutral, probably too little to see on a neutral ramp, so the test needs a pattern
  that separates the two. A `code / 1024` answer means a refit (new composer and RPU). The P8
  canary test (2026-10-13) does not answer it.
- **First canary (2026-10-17): no verdict.** On the C9 (Plex on the Shield, Dolby Vision Cinema
  Home, DV badge on all three files) both steep canaries (chroma coefficients 3.73 on u, u², u³
  and a constant of about −9.3) showed the same uniform green on all seven patches, where either
  normalization predicts a green-to-magenta row with one grey patch; the bt2100 control showed
  the predicted purple. So the TV applies these composers but does not follow the steep curve:
  its composed chroma comes out flat and low, as if clamped. This is the guide's "anything else"
  row. Not recorded: TV firmware, room light.
- **P8 result (2026-10-13):** an LG OLED C9 applies the 8.4 composer in the RPU (canary method in
  [log](docs/ROADMAP_LOG.md)). Not recorded for that test: firmware, picture mode, HDMI path. The
  preset's grey tint looked yellow on the C9, where the libplacebo SDR render predicted lavender
  (mid greys) and olive (dark greys).
